name: 45 A single ESC, 6S
summary: A single-motor 45 A ESC for 3S to 6S, sized for 7-inch builds. Sample data: the supplier and every figure here are fictional.

checked: Rated current, cell range and protocols as stated by the supplier
notChecked: Current rating under our own load test

evidence.summary: One sample inspected and component markings read.
checked: Markings on the MOSFETs, gate driver and MCU
Country of assembly label on the board
notChecked: Whether the chips are genuine, beyond markings

parts.name: Circuit board
parts.role: Carry the power stage, driver and controller, and spread their heat.
parts.whatItDoes: A multi-layer board with thick copper planes. The battery current flows through the planes, so they double as the main heat path.
parts.whyItMatters: Copper weight and layer count decide how much current the board can carry before it overheats. Thin copper is the most common cost cut.
parts.material: FR-4 glass epoxy with heavy copper layers
buyingChecks: Ask for the copper weight of the outer and inner layers
Ask for the board maker and its UL file number
Check the board is conformal coated if the drone flies in dust or spray

parts.name: Power MOSFETs
parts.role: Switch battery current into each motor phase.
parts.whatItDoes: Six transistors arranged as three half bridges. They switch on and off thousands of times a second to build the rotating field the motor needs.
parts.whyItMatters: Their on-resistance sets how much heat the ESC makes. Lower resistance runs cooler and survives longer bursts.
parts.material: Silicon power MOSFETs in surface-mount packages
buyingChecks: Ask for the MOSFET part number and its datasheet
Check the voltage rating leaves headroom over a full 6S pack
Ask how heat leaves the board: copper pour, heatsink or both

parts.name: Gate driver
parts.role: Turns the controller's logic signals into strong pulses that switch the MOSFETs.
parts.whatItDoes: The MCU's outputs are too weak to switch large transistors quickly. The gate driver boosts them so the MOSFETs spend as little time as possible half on, where they waste power.
parts.whyItMatters: A slow or marginal gate driver makes the MOSFETs run hot and can cause failures that look random.
buyingChecks: Ask for the gate driver part number
Check it is rated for the full pack voltage
Ask if the same driver is used across production batches

parts.name: Microcontroller
parts.role: Runs the ESC firmware and decides when to switch each phase.
parts.whatItDoes: A small 32-bit processor reads the throttle command from the flight controller and senses the motor position, then times the switching of each phase.
parts.whyItMatters: The processor decides which firmware the ESC can run, which affects smoothness, telemetry and how the ESC reacts to a stalled motor.
buyingChecks: Ask which firmware ships and whether it can be updated
Check the processor family against your firmware choice
Ask for the firmware version on each batch

parts.name: Input capacitor
parts.role: Absorb voltage spikes on the battery leads.
parts.whatItDoes: A low-impedance electrolytic capacitor soldered across the battery input. It supplies the sharp bursts of current the MOSFETs draw and soaks up the spikes they cause.
parts.whyItMatters: An undersized or fake capacitor lets voltage spikes reach the MOSFETs, which is a leading cause of ESC failure on long battery leads.
buyingChecks: Ask for the capacitor maker, voltage and ESR rating
Check the voltage rating is at least 1.25 times full battery voltage
Ask whether extra capacitance is needed for leads longer than 15 cm

parts.name: Power and phase leads
parts.role: Bring battery current in and send three phases out to the motor.
parts.whatItDoes: Two thick battery leads at one end and three phase leads at the other, in silicone-insulated stranded copper.
parts.whyItMatters: Wire gauge sets voltage drop and heat. Leads that are too thin for the current get hot at the solder joint, where they also fail.
parts.material: Tinned stranded copper with silicone insulation
buyingChecks: Ask for the wire gauge and strand count
Check the insulation is silicone rated to at least 150 C
Pull-test one lead at the solder pad on a sample

parts.name: Thermal pad
parts.role: Carry heat from the MOSFETs into the heatsink.
parts.whatItDoes: A soft, electrically insulating pad pressed between the MOSFET tops and the heatsink. It fills the air gaps that would otherwise block heat.
parts.whyItMatters: A missing or thin pad can double MOSFET temperature. It is cheap to leave out and invisible once the heatsink is on.
parts.material: Silicone thermal pad with ceramic filler
buyingChecks: Ask for the pad's thermal conductivity in W/mK
Check the pad covers every MOSFET on a sample
Ask for the breakdown voltage of the pad

parts.name: Heatsink
parts.role: Move MOSFET heat into the air.
parts.whatItDoes: A finned aluminium block clamped over the MOSFETs. Air from the propeller wash flows between the fins.
parts.whyItMatters: At high current the heatsink decides whether the ESC can hold its rated current for minutes or only seconds.
buyingChecks: Ask for the rated current with and without the heatsink
Check the fins face the airflow in your mounting position
Ask for the alloy and anodising spec

demand.reason: Every brushless motor needs a speed controller. China's export licensing covers ESCs rated at 48 V and 3 kW or more, the same band as heavy-lift motors, and defence buyers reject drones with Chinese parts.

sources.title: Summary of China's drone export controls, Announcement No. 49
Army drone procurement and the ban on Chinese parts, Rediff and Business Standard, 23 Nov 2026
